summary: The recurring Windows WinError 10053 subclass for early-rejected loopback POSTs was repaired by preserving the existing security decision and then draining only bounded, non-chunked request bytes that were never parsed. This prevents normal rejected form bodies from remaining unread at connection teardown without granting action authority or weakening Host, Origin, CSRF or replay protections.

root_cause_scope: Early POST rejections could return before a normal-sized body already sent by the local client was consumed. On Windows this connection-teardown shape was consistent with the repeatedly observed client-side 10053 abort. The repair is deliberately scoped to bounded unparsed rejected bodies and does not claim the separately observed valid /profile/create timeout shared the same cause.
repair: Install one ConsumerShell response-boundary extension using the existing shell composition pattern. After an existing handler decides an eligible early rejection, discard only a non-negative Content-Length within the existing form-size limit and only when Transfer-Encoding is absent. Never parse those bytes, never consume an action token, and preserve the exact response and authority checks.
